title: Finite locally free surjections in a morphism of group extensions
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For $i=1,2$, let $K_i,E_i,Q_i$ be commutative $B$-group schemes, meaning schemes over $B$ with addition, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities. Suppose $0\to K_i\xrightarrow{j_i}E_i\xrightarrow{q_i}Q_i\to0$ is exact as a sequence of sheaves on the big fppf site of $B$ [def-pc-fppf-site]: for every $B$-scheme $U$, $j_i$ identifies $K_i(U)$ with the kernel of $q_i:E_i(U)\to Q_i(U)$, and each section of $Q_i(U)$ lifts to $E_i$ after an fppf covering of $U$. Let $u:K_1\to K_2$, $v:E_1\to E_2$, and $w:Q_1\to Q_2$ be homomorphisms with $v j_1=j_2u$ and $q_2v=wq_1$. If $u$ and $w$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and surjective on underlying points, then $v$ is finite locally free and surjective on underlying points. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness or invertibility hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Form $P=Q_1\times_{Q_2}E_2$, with projections $a:P\to Q_1$ and $b:P\to E_2$. The equation $q_2v=wq_1$ gives $h=(q_1,v):E_1\to P$ and $v=bh$. The morphism $b$ is the base change of $w$ along $q_2$. These assertions follow immediately from the universal property of the fibre product.

source.place: Tag 001V, definition-fibre-product, applied to schemes; agent-written factorization

proof.text: Apply the assumed fppf-local lifting property of $q_1$ to $\mathrm{id}_{Q_1}\in Q_1(Q_1)$. Obtain an fppf covering $\{V_i\to Q_1\}$ and lifts $e_i\in E_1(V_i)$. Put $T_i=P\times_{Q_1}V_i$. The base-change theorem for fppf covers makes $\{T_i\to P\}$ an fppf covering. Write $x_i:T_i\to Q_1$ and $y_i:T_i\to E_2$ for its universal components and still write $e_i$ for the pulled-back lift, so $q_1(e_i)=x_i$ and $q_2(y_i)=w(x_i)$.

source.place: Tag 021O, lemma-fppf (3); universal-section lift from the item hypothesis, written by Q05

proof.text: Since $q_2(y_i-v(e_i))=w(x_i)-w(q_1(e_i))=0$, the kernel hypothesis gives a unique $k_i\in K_2(T_i)$ with $j_2(k_i)=y_i-v(e_i)$. For every $T_i$-scheme $R$, translation $k\mapsto e_i|_R+j_1(k)$ is a bijection from $\{k\in K_1(R):u(k)=k_i|_R\}$ to $\{e\in E_1(R):q_1(e)=x_i|_R,\ v(e)=y_i|_R\}$: the inverse is the unique $k$ with $j_1(k)=e-e_i|_R$, and injectivity of $j_2$ makes $v(e)=y_i|_R$ equivalent to $u(k)=k_i|_R$. These formulas commute with restriction. The fibre-product universal property and fully faithful Yoneda therefore identify $E_1\times_P T_i\to T_i$ with $K_1\times_{K_2,k_i}T_i\to T_i$, as morphisms of schemes over $T_i$.

source.place: Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda; inverse translation formulas and kernel argument written by Q05

proof.text: Apply finite-morphism base change, flat-morphism base change, and local-finite-presentation base change to $u$ and $w$. By the definition of finite locally free, every base change used here is finite locally free. Surjectivity is also stable under base change. Thus the local models for $h$ of step 3 are finite locally free and surjective, and so is $b$ from step 1. The local statements transfer across the displayed isomorphisms (finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation are properties of morphisms, independent of isomorphic presentations).

proof.text: The covering $\{T_i\to P\}$ is fpqc because it is fppf. Descend finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation separately along this very covering. Their three descent statements apply to $h:E_1\to P$ and give these three properties for $h$; hence $h$ is finite locally free. It is also surjective on underlying points: for $z\in P$ choose $t\in T_i$ over $z$ by joint surjectivity, and then a point of $E_1\times_PT_i$ over $t$ by step 4. Its projection to $E_1$ maps to $z$.

source.place: Tags 02LA, lemma-descending-property-finite; 02L2, lemma-descending-property-flat; 02KY, lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation; together Tag 02VO, lemma-descending-property-finite-locally-free; fppf-to-fpqc: topologies.tex Tag 022C; point argument by Q05

proof.text: Finite locally free morphisms are closed under composition, so $v=bh$ is finite locally free. For any point $e_2\in E_2$, surjectivity of $b$ gives $z\in P$ with $b(z)=e_2$, and surjectivity of $h$ gives $e_1\in E_1$ with $h(e_1)=z$; hence $v(e_1)=e_2$. This proves both conclusions with no further hypotheses.
